facts.statement: Goyocephale lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous approximately 76 million years ago.
facts.quote: Goyocephale is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurian ornithischian that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous about 76 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus was first described in 1982 by Altangerel Perle, Teresa Maryańska, and Halszka Osmólska based on a disarticulated skeleton containing most of a skull, parts of the limbs, pelvic girdle, and vertebrae.
facts.quote: It was first described in 1982 by Altangerel Perle, Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska for a disarticulated skeleton with most of a skull, part of the forelimb and hindlimb, some of the pelvic girdle, and some vertebrae.

facts.statement: The genus name Goyocephale means "decorated head", combining the Mongolian word for decorated and the Greek word for head.
facts.quote: Perle et al. named the remains Goyocephale lattimorei, from the Mongolian гоё (goyo), meaning "decorated", and the Ancient Greek κεφαλή (kephale), for head.

facts.statement: The species name lattimorei honors the explorer Owen Lattimore.
facts.quote: The species name honours Owen Lattimore.

facts.statement: Small bony bumps on the posterior edge of the skull roof indicate that Goyocephale possessed small horns in life.
facts.quote: The posterior edge of the skull roof, at the edge of the squamosal bones, has many small bony bumps, which would have been the base of small horns in life.

facts.statement: Goyocephale had a heterodont dentition featuring large caniniform premaxilla teeth, a gap between the premaxilla and maxilla, and regular sub-triangular maxilla teeth.
facts.quote: A feature shared with pachycephalosaurids, Goyocephale had a heterodont dentition, with large caniniform premaxilla teeth, followed by a diastema between the premaxilla and the maxilla, and the regular sub-triangular teeth in the maxilla.

facts.statement: The humerus of Goyocephale is strongly bowed with nearly equal expansion at both the distal and proximal ends.
facts.quote: The humerus is strongly bowed, with a nearly equal expansion on the distal and proximal ends.

facts.statement: Goyocephale likely weighed between 10 and 40 kilograms and measured about 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Goyocephale pesó probablemente 10-40 kilogramos y midió alrededor de 2 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Goyocephale possessed longitudinally oval supratemporal fenestrae with a narrow bridge between them.
facts.quote: Las ventanas supratemporales son longitudinalmente óvales, y el puente entre ellas es estrecho.

facts.statement: A unique feature of Goyocephale is a sinuous lateral skull margin that is particularly prominent above the orbit where the two supraorbitals meet.
facts.quote: Hay solamente algunas características que son peculiares a Goyocephale, éstas incluye el margen lateral sinuoso del cráneo, que es particularmente prominente sobre la órbita donde los dos supraorbitales se encuentran.

facts.statement: Goyocephale is a primitive pachycephalosaurian originally classified in the family Homalocephalidae alongside Homalocephale.
facts.quote: Goyocephale is a primitive pachycephalosaurian, and was originally included in the family Homalocephalidae, which united the genus with Homalocephale, which also has a flat skull roof.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses often treat Homalocephalidae as a paraphyletic group, placing Goyocephale as a branch sister to Pachycephalosauridae or as a primitive member within Pachycephalosauridae.
facts.quote: However, many more recent phylogenetic analyses tend to find Homalocephalidae to be a paraphyletic family, with the genera included simply being consecutive branches sister to Pachycephalosauridae, or as consecutive branches primitive to Prenocephale but within Pachycephalosauridae.

facts.statement: One phylogenetic analysis supports a monophyletic Homalocephalidae, identifying Goyocephale, Homalocephale, and Wannanosaurus as the most derived pachycephalosaurians.
facts.quote: However, one phylogenetic analysis did support a monophyletic Homalocephalidae, with Goyocephale, Homalocephale and Wannanosaurus being the most derived pachycephalosaurians, and their sister taxa being Prenocephale and Tylocephale.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the derived position of Asian pachycephalosaurians like Goyocephale supports a hypothesis that the group evolved in North America before migrating to Asia.
facts.quote: This positioning of all the taxa from Asia as most derived would support that pachycephalosaurians evolved in North America, where they retained their greatest diversity, before migrating to Asia.

facts.statement: The species Goyocephale lattimorei was formally described in 1982 by Perle, Maryańska, and Osmólska based on an incomplete skull, jaws, and fragmentary postcranial material found in Mongolia.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, G. lattimorei, fue descrita formalmente por Perle, Maryańska, y Osmólska en 1982 a partir de un cráneo incompleto, mandíbulas, y de un material postcranial fragmentario encontrado en Mongolia.

facts.statement: The species name honors Owen Lattimore.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra a Owen Lattimore.

facts.statement: Goyocephale is a primitive pachycephalosaurid that was originally placed in the family Homalocephalidae.
facts.quote: Goyocephale es un paquicefalosáurido primitivo y fue originalmente incluido en la familia Homalocephalidae

facts.statement: Many recent phylogenetic analyses suggest that Homalocephalidae is a paraphyletic family, with its genera included either as successive sister branches of Pachycephalosauridae or as primitive branches within Pachycephalosauridae leading to Prenocephale.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, muchos análisis filogenéticos más recientes tienden a encontrar que Homalocephalidae es una familia parafilética, con los géneros incluidos simplemente como ramas consecutivas hermanas de Pachycephalosauridae, o como ramas consecutivas primitivas a Prenocephale pero dentro de Pachycephalosauridae.

facts.statement: One phylogenetic analysis supported a monophyletic Homalocephalidae, identifying Goyocephale, Homalocephale, and Wannanosaurus as the most derived pachycephalosaurids.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un análisis filogenético apoyó un Homalocephalidae monofilético, con Goyocephale, Homalocephale y Wannanosaurus siendo los paquicefalosáuridos más derivados

facts.statement: The placement of Asian taxa as the most derived suggests that pachycephalosaurids may have evolved in North America, where they retained their greatest diversity, before migrating to Asia.
facts.quote: Este posicionamiento de todos los taxones de Asia como la mayoría de los derivados permitiría que los paquicefalosáuridos evolucionaran en América del Norte, donde conservaron su mayor diversidad, antes de migrar a Asia.

facts.statement: Goyocephale lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Goyocephale belongs to the parent group Pachycephalosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Pachycephalosauria

facts.statement: Goyocephale is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
